title: APO Mandarin-Miso Salmon with Sesame Sauce
description: Bagless salmon flakes into a glossy mandarin sauce with a small amount of white miso and toasted sesame oil.
equipment: Anova Precision Oven Gen 1 with food probe, bottom drip pan and middle wire rack

ingredients.name: skinless boneless salmon
ingredients.note: Fully thawed, all pin bones removed; two equal portions no thicker than 3/4 inch.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water without a vegetable seasoning blend.

ingredients.name: mild white miso
ingredients.note: Choose lower-sodium miso and measure level.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Squeeze finely grated ginger and leave out the fibers.

steps.title: Preheat the APO
steps.text: Fill the water tank and install the bottom drip pan. Preheat to 140°F with sous vide mode on, 100% steam, rear element on, top and bottom elements off. Set the food probe target to 139°F.

steps.title: Position the fish
steps.text: Place {salmon} unbagged in the pan on the middle rack. Insert the probe horizontally into the center of the thickest portion. Begin cooking immediately and set a separate 25-minute reminder for the first temperature check; respond sooner if the probe signals.

steps.title: Start the mandarin sauce
steps.text: While the fish cooks, simmer {broth}, {juice} and {ginger} in the HexClad over medium-low for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Make the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and keep it bubbling gently for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish with miso
steps.text: Blend {miso} into a spoonful of the warm sauce until smooth. Whisk it back in with {sesame} off heat.

steps.title: Steam to the probe target
steps.text: Cook in full steam until the probe reaches 139°F, roughly 30–65 minutes from refrigerated, depending on thickness. Start checking after 25 minutes.

steps.title: Check for doneness
steps.text: At 139°F, check the thickest center of each portion for flesh that is opaque all the way through and flakes easily with a fork. If either cue is missing, continue in the 140°F full-steam oven and recheck every 3 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Serve in soft flakes
steps.text: Slide a thin spatula under each portion. Spoon a pool of sauce onto each plate, set the salmon in it and spoon the remaining sauce over the top.

notes: Make ahead: Juice the mandarin and ginger ahead and refrigerate separately. Cook the fish close to serving. The 139–140°F center and flake check apply to the first cook; stored leftovers have a separate reheating endpoint. Option A uses mandarin and ginger. For gentler Option B, replace the juice with smooth pear puree and omit the ginger. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. These thin portions flake apart after freezing and reheating; the sauce freezes well on its own. Fridge reheat: Place one portion and its sauce in a shallow covered dish. Install the APO bottom drip pan and preheat to 325°F, sous vide mode off, 60% steam, rear element on, top and bottom off. Insert the probe in the coldest center and set it to 165°F. Start checking after 12 minutes and heat to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: If previously frozen, thaw in the refrigerator overnight and use the same covered reheating method. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 291 kcal, 27.0 g protein, 3.9 g total carbohydrate, 17.8 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 142 mg sodium. The estimate uses farmed Atlantic salmon. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
